slot.brief: Cleavage of an unsymmetrical ether with excess HI; ask which bond breaks and what alcohol + iodide products form (SN1 vs SN2 pathway shown in figure).

stem: The ether shown is heated with excess $\text{HI}$. Which products and cleavage pathway are expected?
options: Iodobenzene and 1-methylcyclohexanol; cleavage at the aryl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.
Phenol and 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$.
Phenol and 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.
Phenol and 1-methylcyclohexanol; cleavage at the tertiary alkyl–O bond without iodide substitution.

verdicts.working: HI protonates the ether; cleavage occurs at the tertiary alkyl–O bond via SN1. Iodide captures the tertiary carbocation, giving 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane and phenol. The aryl–O bond remains intact.

working:
$\text{1-phenoxy-1-methylcyclohexane} + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{phenol} + \text{1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane}$; protonation followed by C–O cleavage forms a tertiary carbocation; $\text{I}^- $ captures it by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.

Independent check: HI protonates the ether; cleavage occurs at the tertiary alkyl–O bond via SN1. Iodide captures the tertiary carbocation, giving 1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane and phenol. The aryl–O bond remains intact.
solution:
HI protonates the ether, then the tertiary alkyl–O bond cleaves to form a stable tertiary carbocation; the aryl–O bond remains intact.
$$\text{1-phenoxy-1-methylcyclohexane} + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{phenol} + \text{1-iodo-1-methylcyclohexane}$$
Iodide captures the carbocation by an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway.
